name: Verner Osgood
summary: Outside Lakeshire’s smithy, Verner Osgood keeps the forge working. He balances local trade with the Stormwind Guard’s demands for horseshoes, weapons, and armor as gnolls raid the hills.

sections.title: The Anvil of Lakeshire
sections.body: At Lakeshire’s forge, Verner Osgood makes horseshoes and other supplies for the town. His stock is constantly taken to make weapons and armor for the Stormwind Guard. With the kingdom’s forces stretched thin and local garrisons short on supplies, Verner carries much of the burden of keeping Redridge’s defenders equipped.

sections.title: A Plague of Gnolls
sections.body: Gnoll raids threaten Verner’s work as well as the town’s horses. Packs ambush livestock in the Redridge hills and seize working horses that stray beyond Lakeshire. Verner recruits travelers to hunt the marauders and their packleader, Yowler.

faq.answer: Verner Osgood tends the forge in Lakeshire, making metalwork and shoes for horses while meeting the local garrison’s heavy demands for equipment.

faq.q: Why is Verner low on horseshoes and iron?
faq.answer: Iron supplies are continually requisitioned to make weapons and armor for the Stormwind Guard in Redridge, leaving Verner barely enough metal to shoe the town’s horses.

faq.q: What problem does Verner have with the gnolls?
faq.answer: Gnoll raiders near Lakeshire seize Verner’s horses whenever they stray beyond town. He hires travelers to protect his livelihood and take retribution by hunting the packs.

faq.q: Who is Yowler and why does Verner want him dead?
faq.answer: Yowler leads the local gnoll packs in the hills. Verner wants him slain to break the raiders’ coordination and stop them from terrorizing the town and killing his horses.

faq.q: What is Verner's connection to Magistrate Solomon?
faq.answer: Verner works under Magistrate Solomon’s civic authority in Lakeshire, balancing civilian craft with the civic and military needs of the magistrate’s beleaguered administration.

faq.q: Does Verner have family in Stormwind?
faq.answer: Verner shares his surname with Stormwind tradesmen Donal and Basil Osgood, suggesting an established lineage of working-class human craftsmen across the region.

angles.text: As a blacksmith, Verner balances civilian horse shoeing with the harsh quotas imposed by garrison defense.
Lakeshire depends on local craftsmen like Verner to endure while Stormwind’s military aid remains dangerously constrained.
As a human, you share the resilience of Stormwind’s common folk, holding ground against gnolls and shortages alike.
